findings.evidence: c45 cites bin/fm-teardown.sh lines 3894-3896 with the quote "Queued". The evidence snapshot (20261104-062715-yv4m reading-1.json:38) shows those lines were taken from a request and never read from the source. claims.json is an expected and planned deliverable but did not change. The CHANGELOG says the citation is unchecked. `cargo test -p athena-cap-study every_study_follows_the_conventions_and_the_matching_one_validates -- --nocapture` printed 'conventions only' here because the pinned source is absent from the snapshot. Until the citation is checked on the host, the repeated drain report this request is about may not be fixed, and criteria 1 and 3 stay unmet.

findings.summary: The duplicate check matches only on study file and kind, so a new and different contradiction in the same file is silently skipped while any older fix request for that file is open.
findings.evidence: `citing_request` compares only the line 'Source finding: studies/<s>/<file> (<kind>)'. The request said to skip a finding only 'unless an open request already cites it'. Matching on file and kind treats every contradiction in, say, claims.json as the same one. Requests in states that are not closed, including declined and blocked, can hold one back for a long time. A tighter key, such as the claim id or the cited source path and lines from the evidence, would still tolerate the checker's rewording without merging different faults.

summary: The drain half of the request works and is well tested. When the source check fails, drain now builds one high-priority fix request through `StewardRequest::new` that cites each statement and its source. It queues that request with `Athena::queue` and skips any finding an open request already cites. I ran the new unit and integration tests and they pass: one request on the first run, none on the second, and a rewording adds none. The study half is not finished, so the verdict is fail. model.json and intro.json already said reopened returns the item to Queued before this change, and they are untouched. The only citation for that return is claim c45, which points at bin/fm-teardown.sh lines 3894-3896 with the one-word quote "Queued". Those line numbers came from an earlier request and nobody has checked them against the source. The plan said they would be re-cited in claims.json, but claims.json was not changed. The CHANGELOG entry itself says the citation is unchecked and the validation against the real source was never run. When I ran that validation test here, it printed "firstmate-work-handling: conventions only", not "fully validated". So there is no evidence that drain's source check would pass on this study, which is criterion 3 (the producer also reported it unmet). The real source is not in this snapshot, so the citation still needs to be checked on the host, re-cited if it is wrong, and the validation run there.
